comparison: Major disagreement on core findings (C10, C11, C42, C43). OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED due to failure of Bonferroni correction, marginal associations, and lack of replication. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, describing 'convincing evidence' for three immune cell types. This represents the most significant divergence in the evaluations.

Disagreement on MR-BMA findings (C19, C46). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether the analysis ranks spurious associations given marginal primary results. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED without challenging the neutrophil prioritization methodology or conclusions.

Strong disagreement on MVMR and sensitivity analyses (C17, C18, C76, C77). OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED, citing internal contradictions and lack of robustness as undermining causal claims. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as part of careful methodological rigor.

Disagreement on subgroup analyses (C14, C15, C78). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, viewing failure to replicate as potentially indicating spurious original associations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting the authors' explanations for heterogeneity and finding B cell findings appropriately reported.

Disagreement on TWAS findings (C20-C25). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to use of whole-blood rather than oral tissue data and uncertain validity of underlying MR associations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting these as 'interesting results' supporting main findings.

Strong disagreement on therapeutic target claims (C44). OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED, stating gene targets are speculative and conclusions overstate evidence strength. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting translational interpretation within context of overall findings.

Major disagreement on clinical implications (C47, C85, C86). OpenEval rates as UNSUPPORTED, calling translational claims premature and inconsistent with study limitations. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with one explicitly affirming 'significant implications for periodontal care.'

Agreement on statistical limitations (C48, C49, C51). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval commends honest appraisal of limitations including failure of multiple testing correction. Peer reviewers accept these limitations without disputing them.

Agreement on study limitations (C79, C80, C81, C83, C84). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes these limitations substantially impact interpretability. Peer reviewers accept transparent discussion of limitations as appropriate, finding conclusions appropriately tempered.

Agreement on data sourcing and IV selection methodology (C52-C56). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds approach generally sound following established MR practices. Peer reviewers accept study design and data utilization, characterizing work as 'carefully done.'

Agreement on statistical methodology (C12, C74, C75). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds comprehensive and appropriate methods despite noting sophisticated methods cannot overcome marginal primary associations. Peer reviewers accept handling of heterogeneity and quality control.

Disagreement on reverse causality findings (C16). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN overall for subgroup analyses, viewing absence of reverse causality as reassuring but insufficient to validate forward causal claims. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, implicitly accepting this strengthens causal inference.

Agreement on TWAS methodology (C58, C59, C60, C104-C106). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds statistical rigor appropriate but notes fundamental limitation of whole-blood data. Peer reviewers accept TWAS findings without raising methodological concerns.

OpenEval rates background claims (C1-C7) as SUPPORTED, finding them well-supported by appropriate citations providing necessary context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval rates neutrophil biology contextual claims (C26-C35) as SUPPORTED, finding them well-supported with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these biological context claims.
OpenEval rates NKT cell and dendritic cell contextual claims (C36-C41) as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate citation support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval rates study rationale and design justification claims (C8, C63, C65-C73) as SUPPORTED, finding appropriate motivation for MR approach. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological justification claims.
